Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Presenting problem: Recurrent, relapsing episodes over ~1–2 months of right-hand paresthesia (pins-and-needles), transient right arm weakness, and intermittent leg/gait weakness; episodes initially infrequent, now occurring up to a few times per day; each episode lasts days with complete resolution between episodes. Associated fatigue and intermittent nausea. Asymptomatic during consultation.
- Immediate clinical concern and action from transcript: GP working diagnosis = possible transient ischemic attack (TIA)/mini-stroke due to lateralized focal neurological deficits and positive family history for carotid disease → urgent referral to TIA clinic arranged.
- Relevant diagnostic reasoning from DDx consistent with transcript:
  - Multiple sclerosis (relapsing–remitting demyelinating disease): High likelihood per DDx — fits young adult age, relapsing-remitting focal sensory and motor deficits lasting days with full recovery, fatigue. (No imaging or CSF yet.)
  - Hemiplegic migraine: Medium likelihood per DDx — episodic focal neurological deficits with nausea and transient motor dysfunction could represent migrainous aura, though headache was not reported.
  - TIA / recurrent TIAs from vascular cause: Medium likelihood per DDx — lateralized transient deficits and family history raise concern, but duration (days) and young age make classic TIA less typical.
- Conflict noted: GP prioritized urgent exclusion of vascular cause (TIA clinic referral). DDx (diagnostic reasoning tool) ranks multiple sclerosis as most likely etiology. Both diagnostic considerations are documented; difference in leading consideration — "conflict noted."

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Multiple sclerosis — High likelihood
  - Justification: Young adult with relapsing–remitting unilateral sensory symptoms and transient motor weakness/gait disturbance lasting days with complete resolution; associated fatigue; pattern fits relapsing–remitting demyelination. No MRI/CSF confirmation yet.
- Hemiplegic migraine (complex migraine with motor aura) — Moderate likelihood
  - Justification: Episodic transient unilateral sensory and motor deficits with nausea and transient motor dysfunction (difficulty holding cup) could represent motor aura; absence of reported headache and atypical high frequency are opposing points.
- Transient ischemic attack (TIA) / recurrent TIAs — Moderate likelihood
  - Justification: Lateralized transient deficits and family history of carotid disease prompted GP to treat as urgent vascular concern and refer to TIA clinic. Episodes lasting several days are atypical for classic TIA; vascular risk factors reportedly absent and no imaging yet.
